title: Effectiveness of a Jumper's Knee Strap as an Adjunct to Exercise Therapy in Individuals with Patellar Tendinopathy: A Randomized Controlled Trial
summary:
Pain in the tendon located just below the kneecap is a common problem in physically active individuals. In addition to exercise-based treatment, special straps worn below the kneecap are frequently used to reduce pain during physical activity. However, it is still unclear how effective these straps actually are.
The aim of this study is to investigate whether wearing such a strap in addition to a structured exercise program can reduce pain and improve knee function and physical performance.
A total of 26 physically active adults with persistent pain in the tendon below the kneecap will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. Both groups will complete the same 12-week exercise program. One group will receive a strap designed to provide the intended effect, while the other group will receive a visually identical strap that is not expected to have a therapeutic effect.
Pain, daily function, sports-related function, and thigh muscle strength will be assessed before the intervention and again after 4, 8, and 12 weeks.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Ultrasound-confirmed patellar tendinopathy
Activity-related anterior knee pain for at least 3 months
Positive palpation findings at the inferior pole of the patella
VISA-P-G score < 80 points
Reproducible pain during the Single-Leg Decline Squat Test
Regular participation in sports activities (minimum of 2 lower-extremity training sessions per week)
Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
Other causes of anterior knee pain (e.g., patellofemoral pain syndrome, meniscal pathology, ligament injuries, iliotibial band syndrome, plica syndrome)
Previous surgery on the affected knee
Acute knee trauma
Inflammatory or systemic diseases
Pregnancy
Corticosteroid injection within the previous 6 months
Regular use of pain medication or anti-inflammatory medication
Known latex allergy
